name: Iqra Fund
mission: Iqra Fund provides preschool programs for communities to teach children ages four to six years old basic language, social, and formal learning skills to help them succeed in primary school.
programs: Access to Higher Education and Career Pathways
theoryOfChange: Iqra Fund has a published Theory of Change, which states: "{if} girls have an education, communities thrive, nations flourish, and overall planetary health improves." This framework explains that for the first generation of girls in northern Pakistan, access to quality education will break the intergenerational cycle of poverty, lead to community development, and strengthen the overall health of the region. The strategic priorities supporting this theory include Community Engagement, Teacher Training & Development, Learning Environments, Student Success, and Access to Higher Education and Career Pathways. The founder and CEO, Genevieve Walsh, designed this theory of change to clearly communicate the organization's model and vision for long-term impact.

rich_narrative.summary: Iqra Fund focuses on improving access to early education and primary schooling for children, particularly girls, in underserved remote communities in Pakistan. <cite id="[2]">Founded in 2011</cite>, the organization works closely with local villages to build educational infrastructure, train teachers, and support early childhood education. In FY2024, Iqra Fund reported <cite id="[7]">Total Revenue of $1,029,954</cite>, following total revenue of <cite id="[3]">$991,974 in FY2023</cite> driven primarily by <cite id="[3]">$985,338 in individual and institutional contributions</cite>. The organization maintains an efficient fiscal structure with a <cite id="[1]">85.9% program expense Ratio</cite> in FY2024 and an <cite id="[1]">85.9% rating baseline from Charity Navigator</cite>, which surpasses the <cite id="[1]">75% industry standard</cite>. Iqra Fund operates as a <cite id="[2]">Zakat-eligible entity</cite>, providing Muslim donors an opportunity to fulfill religious obligations through educational sponsorship and community capacity building. While its operational scope is geographically focused relative to larger global education funds, its lean cost structure allows for targeted, high-impact intervention.
